scope: Theorem 3.1 (Mixed height limits) of the manuscript “The critical correlation exponent of the planar XY model” (preprints/The-critical-correlation-exponent-of-the-planar-XY-model-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 216 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e58587be77cd0256), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed geometry above and every a(b) > 0, the massless height law with primary hard pins has Gaussian Laplace and moment limits for fixed bounded, piecewise continuous density smears. On a component meeting a pin, the covariance is the inverse of a−1 EU on HU,p. On an unpinned component this assertion concerns mean-free smears. Its fractional mean modulo 2π is asymptotically uniform and independent of the mean-free Gaussian field. Adding a fixed finite-rank nonnegative quadratic penalty in box averages gives the corresponding Gaussian law. If the penalty controls every unpinned component constant, lattice translations are summed and the limiting constants are integrated; the result is an ordinary, unprojected Gaussian law. The assertions include energy-approximable shifts and hold along every admissible primary mesh sequence.
